name: Datum Pipe
tagline: Pipe stress analysis on the desktop: displacements, support loads, nozzle loads and code stresses, with an automatic isometric.
for: Piping, stress, mechanical, process and plant engineers, consultants and students.
about: Datum Pipe works out how a piping system moves and what it pushes on when it heats up, carries its weight, holds its pressure and meets wind or an earthquake. You type the piping as a table of elements, the way a stress engineer marks up an isometric (or import a piping component file from a design tool), and it appears in 3D as you type: pipes at their true diameter, bends, tees, reducers, valves, flanges and supports.

Put on the supports (one-way rests, gaps, friction and spring hangers it sizes for you), the temperatures, pressures and equipment movements; the load cases are built for you. Analyze solves every case with Datum Pipe's own 3D pipe element solver, checks the stresses using the published equations of the process piping code (ASME B31.3), the power piping code (ASME B31.1) or the European piping standard (EN 13480-3), and shows the results on the model, in tables of displacements, support loads and nozzle loads, on an automatic isometric drawing and in a printed stress report. Allowable stresses are your inputs, Help › Verification solves benchmark problems with known answers in front of you, and Help › Sources says where every equation is published.

steps.title: Route the piping
steps.text: Type each element's From node, To node and lengths in the table, or import a piping component file; pick the pipe, material, line conditions and component (bend, tee, reducer, valve, flange). Type values with their units if you like (20 ft, 150 mm). It draws in 3D at once, and analyses as you go.

steps.title: Support and load it
steps.text: Add anchors, rests (one-way, with gaps and friction), guides, line stops, spring hangers and nozzle points; set up to three operating temperatures and pressures, the hydrotest, equipment movements, wind and static seismic.

steps.title: Check and report
steps.text: Analyze, see the stress ratios on the model, read the support and nozzle loads, and print the stress report with the isometric and the equilibrium checks.

highlights: An element table that draws the piping in 3D as you type: true diameters, insulation, bends, tees, reducers, valves, flanges and support symbols
Import of plain-text piping component files (.pcf) from design tools
Pipe sizes ½" to 24" in every schedule, five piping materials with properties against temperature and their sources, and your own sizes and materials

Anchors, one-way rests, guides, line stops and restraints with gaps and friction, skewed restraints, springs, spring hangers sized from your spring table, constant-force supports and imposed equipment movements
Load cases built for you: sustained, operating, expansion range, hydrotest, and wind and static seismic as occasional cases

Code stresses calculated using the equations of the process piping code: hoop stress and minimum wall (straight pipe, bends at their intrados, both ends of reducers), sustained stress, the displacement stress range and occasional stress, with PASS or FAIL at every point

Support loads for the civil team, nozzle loads in the nozzle's own axes, and steam turbine, compressor and pump nozzle checks against their standards' published criteria; flange leakage by the equivalent pressure method; relief valve thrust at an open discharge as an occasional load; vessel and tank nozzle flexibility from your stiffness values; bellows expansion joints with their pressure thrust; wind by height and occasional loads in both directions
An automatic isometric drawing with dimensions, node numbers and result tags, and a printed stress report
Help › Verification: benchmark problems with known answers solved in front of you, and an equilibrium check after every solve; Help › Sources: where every equation is published
Pressure vessels in the same app: shells and heads, MAWP, test pressure and weights
Dynamics: natural frequencies and mode shapes animated in 3D, a response spectrum checked as an occasional load, and the response to a load at a frequency
